briefs.shoulder-rom:
Shoulder Pain

tendon vs joint by range of motion · cuff, impingement and biceps · red flags and referred pain · never a slingIs passive motion preserved, and what has the patient already tried?

DiagnosisManagementPractice
Bottom line

Sort every painful shoulder by range of motion:

  • Active lost, passive kept: muscle or tendon (rotator cuff tendinopathy or tear, impingement, biceps tendinitis).
  • Both lost: the joint (adhesive capsulitis, glenohumeral osteoarthritis, a septic joint).
  • Normal shoulder exam: the pain comes from the neck, the heart or the diaphragm.

Treat tendon pain on the lowest rung not yet tried, usually in this order:

  • Activity change with an NSAID (nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug).
  • Physical therapy, if not improving in 2 to 4 weeks.
  • Injection, then MRI (magnetic resonance imaging), then surgery.

Rest never means immobilize: a sling causes atrophy, and adhesive capsulitis can set in within weeks. Tell the patient what to do, not only what to avoid.

Diagnosis
Defining findings Cuff tendinopathy or impingement – overhead use, painful arc, active motion down only; empty can, Neer or Hawkins positive · Full-thickness cuff tear – weakness more than pain, cannot raise the arm overhead, drop arm positive; traumatic in the young, degenerative in the old · Biceps tendinitis – anterior pain, bicipital groove tenderness, pain on resisted elbow flexion and supination, in a patient still doing the offending activity · Adhesive capsulitis – active and passive motion down; diabetes, hypothyroidism; follows immobilization · Glenohumeral osteoarthritis – active and passive motion down with crepitus in an older patient; prior dislocation is the risk factor · Septic arthritis or bursitis (emergency) – fever, red, swollen shoulder; intravenous drug use, diabetes, rheumatoid arthritis; aspirate before antibiotics
Maneuver and nerve (each maneuver isolates its own muscle group) Empty can (Jobe) – supraspinatus (abduction) · Resisted external rotation – infraspinatus and teres minor · Resisted internal rotation – subscapularis · Anterior dislocation – axillary nerve: lateral deltoid numbness, weak abduction · Scapular winging – long thoracic nerve · Supraspinatus and infraspinatus atrophy – suprascapular nerve
Management and treatment
Management ladder: cuff and biceps tendon pain
TierInterventionEscalate when
1Activity modification (stop the throwing and lifting) and an NSAID; no slingNot improving in 2 to 4 weeks
2Physical therapy: strengthen the cuff and scapular stabilizers to open the subacromial space; relative rest plus progressive loadingPain persists despite therapy
3Corticosteroid injection (subacromial for cuff pain): short-term relief only; never through suspected infectionStill failing, or a full-thickness tear suspected
4MRI, then surgery; X-ray only for trauma or failed therapyTop rung
By diagnosis Full-thickness tear – MRI · Septic joint – aspirate before antibiotics · Sling – only for dislocation or fracture
Practice
  1. 58-year-old man has 2 months of right shoulder pain pain arcs between 60 and 120 degrees of abduction active abduction limited; passive abduction full Paints ceilings for work Afebrile · empty can test painful · Neer test positive → Rotator cuff tendinopathy → active motion lost with passive motion kept is a tendon problem: rotator cuff tendinopathy; relative rest and physical therapy
  2. 62-year-old woman with diabetes has 4 months of shoulder stiffness both active and passive motion lost in every plane external rotation most limited Wore a sling for a wrist fracture Afebrile · no crepitus · strength normal within the motion she has → Adhesive capsulitis → active and passive motion both lost points to the joint; diabetes and immobilization favor adhesive capsulitis
  3. 70-year-old man cannot lift his right arm overhead cannot initiate abduction drop-arm test positive: the arm falls from 90 degrees Weakness worse than pain since a fall Afebrile · passive motion full · no neck pain → Full-thickness rotator cuff tear → a positive drop-arm test is a full-thickness rotator cuff tear: MRI, which is ordered here and not for tendinopathy
  4. 55-year-old man with diabetes has a hot, swollen right shoulder refuses all movement, active or passive visible effusion Pain began 2 days ago Fever, T 38.9 °C · HR 108/min · white cells 16,000/mm³ → Septic arthritis → fever, effusion and refusal of all movement is septic arthritis: aspirate before antibiotics, and never inject steroid into it
  5. 48-year-old man has right shoulder pain radiating below the elbow numbness of the thumb neck extension and rotation reproduce the pain Shoulder range of motion full and painless Afebrile · biceps reflex reduced on the right → C5–C6 radiculopathy → pain past the elbow with thumb numbness and a normal shoulder exam is a C5 to C6 radiculopathy; Spurling is positive
  6. 60-year-old man has left shoulder pain when he climbs stairs pain on exertion, relieved within minutes by rest diaphoresis with the episodes Smoker with hypertension BP 152/90 mm Hg · HR 84/min · shoulder examination normal → Referred cardiac pain → exertional shoulder pain with a normal shoulder exam is referred cardiac pain: ECG (electrocardiogram)
  7. 58-year-old man treated for a painful arc returns at 3 weeks has kept his arm in the sling ever since passive motion now starting to stiffen Was given a sling at the first visit Afebrile · painful arc persists → Continued sling immobilization → continued sling immobilization is how adhesive capsulitis follows a cuff problem; slings are for dislocation and fracture
  8. 26-year-old man has 3 weeks of anterior right shoulder pain tender over the bicipital groove still throwing weekly: pitches in a league every weekend No treatment yet Afebrile · pain on resisted supination with the elbow flexed → Activity modification plus NSAIDs → the least-intensive step comes first: activity modification and an NSAID (nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug); injection and surgery come much later
  9. 26-year-old man, a pitcher, has persistent anterior shoulder pain still painful after 6 weeks of activity modification and NSAIDs tender over the bicipital groove No weakness, locking or night pain Afebrile · range of motion full · strength normal → Physical therapy → not improving after 2 to 4 weeks of activity change and an NSAID: physical therapy is the next rung, before injection or MRI
  10. 62-year-old man felt a pop in his right arm while lifting a box bulge in the mid upper arm when he flexes mild ache, little weakness Elbow crease not tender Afebrile · supination strength nearly normal → Long head of biceps rupture → a proximal (long head) rupture leaves a bulge in the mid arm and is treated without surgery in older adults
  11. 26-year-old man has anterior right shoulder pain after weekend throwing pain reproduced by resisted supination with the elbow flexed tender over the bicipital groove No clicking or locking Afebrile · painful arc absent → Biceps tendinitis → groove tenderness with pain on resisted supination and elbow flexion is biceps tendinitis
  12. 45-year-old man has anterior shoulder pain with overhead work strength normal on resisted abduction painful arc of abduction No groove tenderness Afebrile · a positive Hawkins test · passive range of motion full → Subacromial impingement → a positive Hawkins test with a painful arc is subacromial impingement, part of the cuff tendinopathy spectrum
  13. 45-year-old man has sudden antecubital pain after lifting a heavy cabinet weak supination of the forearm gap palpable above the elbow crease Bruising spreads into the forearm the next day Afebrile · biceps hook test abnormal → Urgent orthopedic referral for surgical repair → a distal biceps rupture is repaired surgically, unlike a proximal one: urgent orthopedic referral
Transferable rule

Range of motion sorts tendon from joint before any test. The next step is usually the next rung not yet tried, and every instruction to rest says what to do instead.
